verified_fixes.detail: Service-role auth check present and correct — blocks all non-service-role callers with 401. Residual error leakage in catch block (detail field) found during audit and fixed: catch block now logs to console.error only, response returns { error: 'Internal server error' } with no detail field. Deployed.

Both tables have RLS enabled. Policy 'Service role only' (FOR ALL TO service_role USING(true) WITH CHECK(true)) is present on both. No anon or authenticated access exists. Pipeline cron reads succeed via service_role.

Old open policy 'authenticated can read pipeline logs' is gone. New policy 'Admins can read pipeline logs' (SELECT TO authenticated WHERE is_admin=true) is the only policy. Pipeline write functions (fn_run_post_pipeline_stabilisation, fn_pipeline_healthcheck) are SECURITY DEFINER owned by postgres — bypass RLS entirely. No write regression confirmed.

Old open policy dropped. Two correct policies live: 'Service role full access on snapshots' (ALL TO service_role) and 'Admins can read snapshots' (SELECT TO authenticated WHERE is_admin=true). Snapshot-writing functions are SECURITY DEFINER / postgres — bypass RLS safely. No regression.

Policy 'Anyone can insert start_sit decisions' is gone. Anon INSERT confirmed removed. Remaining: service_role ALL, authenticated INSERT, anon+authenticated SELECT, authenticated SELECT (duplicate — see regressions).
Duplicate 'Service role can manage system state' dropped. Remaining: 'Service role full access to system_state' (ALL) and 'Admins can read system state' (SELECT WHERE is_admin=true). Clean.

Duplicate 'Service role full player_prices' dropped. Remaining: 'Service role full access player_prices' (ALL) and 'Public read player_prices' (SELECT TO anon,authenticated — intentional for frontend price display).
Duplicate 'Service role manages start sit decisions' dropped. Single service_role ALL policy 'Service role full access to start_sit_decisions' remains.

Both tables now have 'Service role full access' (ALL TO service_role) policies. Existing authenticated SELECT policies retained. Signal pipeline functions (fn_generate_player_signals, fn_build_player_signal_summary) are SECURITY DEFINER / postgres — defense-in-depth confirmed.

Old SELECT-only service_role policy dropped. New 'Service role full access weekly plans cache' (ALL TO service_role) live. Admin authenticated INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE policies retained. No write regression.

Old misnamed authenticated policy dropped. 'Service role full access' (ALL TO service_role) is the only policy. Rankings RPCs (get_rankings_free, get_rankings_premium, get_captain_recommendations_free) are SECURITY DEFINER / postgres — read from this table safely via RLS bypass. No frontend regression.
No error.message in any response. Both commit_price_ingest error path and outer catch return generic 'Request failed'.
Catch block logs to console.error and returns generic 'Request failed'. No raw message in response.
Both catch paths return generic 'Request failed'. Raw errMsg no longer surfaced in responses.
Catch block returns generic 'Request failed'. Return URL validated against ALLOWED_RETURN_ORIGINS allowlist — open redirect closed.
Catch block returns generic 'Request failed'. No raw error message surfaced.

Anon INSERT policy dropped. 'Authenticated users can insert analytics events' (INSERT TO authenticated) is live. Service role full access retained. Note: unauthenticated visitor analytics to Supabase now silently fail — PostHog is unaffected. See product note in regressions.

CONFIRMED PLATFORM LIMITATION. Both schema-level REVOKE and function-level REVOKE were attempted. proacl on net.http_get and net.http_post shows '=X/supabase_admin' — PUBLIC EXECUTE is granted by supabase_admin, which is the platform owner. This grant is re-applied automatically and cannot be overridden by postgres-role migrations. anon and authenticated retain EXECUTE on net functions. This is a Supabase-managed infrastructure privilege — not fixable via SQL migrations.

regressions.issue: Two duplicate SELECT policies for authenticated role remain: 'Anyone can read start sit decisions' (anon+authenticated USING(true)) and 'Authenticated users can read start_sit decisions' (authenticated USING(true)). Redundant, not a security risk.
regressions.risk: None. Both allow identical access. Minor policy hygiene.
regressions.fix: DROP POLICY "Authenticated users can read start_sit decisions" ON public.start_sit_decisions;

regressions.issue: logEvent() uses the anon Supabase client. Now that INSERT requires authenticated role, unauthenticated page views silently fail to log to analytics.events. The code handles this gracefully. PostHog tracking is unaffected.
regressions.risk: Loss of anonymous visitor DB analytics. No security risk — this is an intentional product behavior change from the hardening fix.
regressions.fix: Accept as intentional if authenticated-only analytics is desired. Or add a constrained anon INSERT policy. Or route through an edge function.

platform_limitations.finding: net.http_get and net.http_post have PUBLIC EXECUTE (=X) granted by supabase_admin. This is a Supabase platform-managed privilege. Both REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA and REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION were attempted — neither persists. The platform re-applies this grant automatically. This cannot be fixed via SQL migrations in a hosted Supabase project.
platform_limitations.risk: Authenticated and anon roles can call net.http_get/http_post from SQL context. In practice, anon users cannot execute arbitrary SQL, and authenticated users would need a SECURITY INVOKER function or direct psql access. RLS on all tables already blocks data exfiltration via SQL. The risk is theoretical in normal app usage.
platform_limitations.recommendation: Document as accepted platform limitation. If pg_net must be restricted, contact Supabase support or use a dedicated Supabase project with custom network policies.

final_state.net_schema_function_execute_for_anon_aut: PLATFORM LIMITATION — cannot be revoked via migration

recommendations.action: Drop duplicate SELECT policy 'Authenticated users can read start_sit decisions' on public.start_sit_decisions — cosmetic hygiene only.
Decide on anonymous analytics: accept loss of unauthenticated visitor DB events (PostHog still captures them), or add a constrained anon INSERT policy.
net.http_get / net.http_post PUBLIC EXECUTE cannot be revoked — Supabase platform limitation. Document as accepted risk. No practical exploit path exists for normal app users.

admin.command_logs has RLS enabled with zero service_role policies. Current writer (admin.get_system_health) is SECURITY DEFINER / postgres so writes bypass RLS. Monitor for future direct service_role writes — they will be blocked.
